claims.claim: In the declared finite graph fixture, under B_off=0, R=0, and identical edge-examination accounting, bidirectional BFS with direct online predecessor access solves additional sampled instances at fixed tight online budgets where forward BFS with a visited set does not.
claims.scope: M in {30,300,3000}; 200 seeded queries per M; corrected edge-examination accounting; caps through 640 for frontier measurements
limits: one arithmetic graph family and query seed
forward BFS is a strong simple baseline, not a theorem-level optimum over all successor-only algorithms
predecessor access is the specific changed transition capability
the absolute ultimate feasible-set difference is not established

claims.claim: Within the same B_off=0, R=0 contract, emulating predecessor access using only the original successor operations requires substantial online scanning and does not reproduce the native bidirectional frontier at the tight budgets tested.
claims.scope: same graph/query fixture; exhaustive predecessor discovery charged one tick per candidate-edge examination
limits: the emulation is generic exhaustive scanning and may not be optimal for every successor-only encoding
different graph families may admit cheaper successor-only inverse reasoning
claims.interpretation: under this resource contract, direct predecessor access is not reproduced by the tested successor-only reorganization
claims.next_discriminating_test: Repeat on independent graph families and include stronger successor-only inverse representations with all construction/use costs charged online.

claims.claim: The observed frontier shift should not be interpreted as an absolute difference in ultimate solvability: at sufficiently high online budgets, the successor-only baseline can recover the sampled instances, while the exhaustive emulation also eventually succeeds on tested finite cases.
claims.scope: sampled finite workloads; high-budget spot checks
limits: does not characterize the entire infinite instance family

claims.claim: Mechanism change should be evaluated by measured feasible-set and Pareto-frontier shifts under a matched execution contract, not by the category name itself.
limits: the present result establishes one specific frontier shift, not a universal law about all mechanism changes
different mechanism definitions can embed different amounts of computation
claims.next_discriminating_test: Separate direct information-access advantages from hidden computation embedded in the new mechanism and replicate across graph families.
